topic: How GPS finds you (Selective Availability first)

lines.say: Until two thousand, America made public GPS wrong on purpose, enough to put you a street away from where you really were.
lines.show: Until 2000, America made public GPS *wrong on purpose,* enough to put you a street away from [where you really were.]

lines.say: Then President Clinton ordered that error switched off, and overnight, ordinary receivers could find the right road.
lines.show: Then President Clinton ordered that error *switched off,* and overnight, ordinary receivers could find [the right road.]

lines.say: Today your phone can find the street you're on. And the GPS satellites have no idea you exist.
lines.show: Today your phone can find the street you're on. And the GPS satellites have [no idea you exist.]

lines.say: Your phone never sends anything to them. It only listens.
lines.show: Your phone never sends anything to them. It [only listens.]

lines.say: About thirty GPS satellites orbit the Earth, carrying super precise clocks. They keep broadcasting where they are, and exactly when each signal left.
lines.show: About *30 GPS satellites* orbit the Earth, carrying super precise clocks. They keep broadcasting where they are, and exactly [when each signal left.]

lines.say: The signals travel at the speed of light, so how long each one takes tells your phone how far away that satellite is.
lines.show: The signals travel at the *speed of light,* so how long each one takes tells your phone [how far away that satellite is.]

lines.say: One distance puts you somewhere on a giant sphere. Add more satellites, and the spheres overlap at one spot. A fourth one fixes your phone's clock, which is nowhere near as precise.
lines.show: One distance puts you somewhere on a giant sphere. Add more satellites, and the spheres *overlap at one spot.* A fourth one fixes your phone's clock, which is [nowhere near as precise.]

lines.say: So GPS isn't tracking you from space. The satellites only say where they are. Your phone works out where you are.
lines.show: So GPS isn't tracking you from space. The satellites only say where they are. [Your phone works out where you are.]
